После подсчета более 99% бюллетеней он более чем на три процента опережает выигравшего первый тур выборов 45-летнего сенатора Флавиу Болсонару, сына осужденного экс-президента Бразилии. Лула получает 51,8% голосов, Болсонару — 48,2%. За действующего главу государства отдали голоса более 64 млн избирателей, сына бывшего президента поддержали чуть менее 60 млн. Это первый случай в истории Бразилии, когда выборы выигрывает кандидат, проигравший первый тур голосования. title: Brazil runoff live updates: Lula has defeated Bolsonaro, electoral court announces
text: 20.22 EDT Lula defeats Bolsonaro to win historic fourth term Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has staged a dramatic election fightback and defeated his far-right opponent Flávio Bolsonaro to claim a historic fourth term in power. With nearly 99% of votes counted the 80-year-old leftist received 51.75% of the vote to his 45-year-old rival’s 48.25%, Tom Phillips and Tiago Rogero report. Lula narrowly lost the first round of the election to Bolsonaro in early October, casting his political future into doubt and plunging progressive Brazilians into three weeks of despair. Never, since the return of democracy in the 1980s, has the first round runner-up won the second vote. But Lula did precisely that on Sunday, prompting joyous scenes on the streets of São Paulo, where he had been following the count, and at the hotel where he was watching the count. For Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, the victory represents a sensational final chapter in a storied political career that began when he emerged as a union leader in São Paulo’s industrial suburbs in the late 1970s. See the full story here: Lula wins fourth term as Brazil’s president over Flávio Bolsonaro Read more
author: Adam Fulton (now); Marina Dunbar (earlier)

title: Brazil election 2026: Full second round results as Lula wins comeback against Flávio Bolsonaro
text: Brazil Brazil election 2026: Full second round results as Lula wins comeback against Flávio Bolsonaro After a shock defeat in the first round, the incumbent Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has turned the election around to win the runoff. Live blog: latest analysis and reaction Seán Clarke and Tom Phillips Sun 25 Oct 2026 20.15 EDT First published on Sun 25 Oct 2026 15.37 EDT Share Live second round results Last updated at 21:00:41 BRT With 88.7% of districts counted Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva 51.52% Workers' party (PT) | 56,506,197 votes Flávio Bolsonaro 48.48% Liberal party (PL) | 53,164,037 votes Guardian graphic. Source: TSE Results by state How the election works Brazil’s president is elected purely by the popular vote. A winning candidate needs one more vote than 50% of votes cast; there is no role for the parliament and no electoral college. Because no candidate achieved 50% in the first round on 4 October, the two leading candidates go into a runoff. One of them is Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , the incumbent leftwing president, commonly known as Lula. title: Australia politics live: Taylor says alleged attack on Helen Haines ‘unfathomable’; Steggall calls Indi MP ‘matriarch of crossbench’ as parliament hears emotional tributes
text: 19.05 EDT Albanese pays tribute to Helen Haines in parliament The prime minister, Anthony Albanese , has offered his support and well wishes for the independent MP for Indi, Helen Haines , after she was allegedly attacked in her electorate last week. He addressed the House of Representatives this morning: The shock from what happened last Monday is like a stone in our hearts. Haines’ seat has been filled with an orange cockatoo sign as many MPs wear flowers on their lapel in tribute to the MP. We look across to the member for Indi’s place, and despite ourselves, half expect to see a face, like a trick that the heart plays on the mind, if only to grant us a moment’s respite from the truth. Right now, our friend and colleague is in hospital, grievously injured. The shape of her life and her family’s lives changed for ever. Anthony Albanese. Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP Many politicians are wearing orange and white as a tribute to Haines. An orange cockatoo sign has been placed on her seat in the House of Representatives because the symbol is synonymous with Haines.
